notes: A TAX-LAW CHANGE, WHICH DOES NOT AFFECT SBS TODAY. Ghana's Value Added Tax Act, 2025 (Act 1151) took effect on 1 January 2026 and made the NHIL (2.5%) and the GETFund levy (2.5%) reclaimable input tax on purchases. They were not before. The School is not VAT-registered, so it reclaims no input VAT and nothing in your books changes. This release is here so the rule is right in the ledger before it ever matters, and so that any unit that does register is handled correctly from the day it does. IF THAT EVER CHANGES, the app now decides which rule applies from the date on the bill, not from a setting. A bill dated from 1 January 2026 reclaims the whole 20%; one dated before it reclaims only the 15% VAT proper, exactly as it did when it was entered. Nothing already posted is restated, and entering a 2025 invoice today still gets the 2025 treatment. THE VAT RETURN STILL SHOWS VAT, NHIL AND GETFUND SEPARATELY, as the GRA's form requires, even though the three are now one reclaimable charge. The Ghana Tourism Levy is unaffected by the Act — still 1%, still on the value before VAT, still remitted to the Ghana Tourism Authority. NO DATA RESHAPE: this installs straight over the previous version. Please still take a backup first — Backup & Export, Back up now.
